packageRules.description: The weekly automerge batch. Patch and minor for everything OUTSIDE the never-alone list below, in one grouped pull request, merged without a human once the five required checks pass. Two things about this rule are load-bearing. It is FIRST because packageRules are applied in array order and later rules override earlier ones (mergeChildConfig), so every rule below wins over it. And the exclusion is a negated matchDepNames list rather than the removed excludePackageNames: in a list of only negative patterns, a dependency matches when none of them match it. matchDepNames, not matchPackageNames, because they are different matchers over different fields — node in .github/workflows/ci.yml has depName node but packageName actions/node-versions, so matchPackageNames would silently miss it and automerge a Node bump. A dependency is on the never-alone list below either because something written in this tree states a reason a bump could invalidate, or because its failure mode is invisible to all five required checks.

NEVER ALONE — framework. AGENTS.md: Turbopack leaks memory, dev is pinned to --webpack, and Turbopack must be re-tested after every Next.js upgrade (#161). eslint belongs here because #47 proved it cannot move without eslint-config-next: split across two groups it sat red for eight weeks with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs'). typescript belongs here for the same relation to the same package, established by a different incident: typescript-eslint arrives transitively as eslint-config-next -> typescript-eslint, it declares peerDependencies.typescript as ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0", and it reads ts.Extension.Cjs at module load, before any eslint.config.mjs is consulted — so a minor to TypeScript 6.1 already puts the parser outside its declared peer range and no config change avoids it (#1051, platform.md). The error string is #47's and the cause is not: that one was a config/plugin split, this one is a version gap between typescript-eslint and the compiler — do not merge the two incidents on the strength of the message. No schedule — these reach the user promptly rather than waiting for the Monday window. The empty schedule is redundant while the exclusion list above is complete, and is here so that 'unscheduled' stays true by construction if the two lists ever drift.

NEVER ALONE — TanStack Query. AGENTS.md makes it an invariant: TanStack Query for data fetching, through the shared list-screen primitives. TanStack Table is kept in matchDepNames deliberately even though nothing depends on it today (#821, ADR-0001 chose it and it was never installed) — the rule costs nothing while the package is absent and is already correct if it is ever added. The reason this one is never-alone is not a version written down anywhere — it is that its failure mode is invisible to every required check we have. Lint, typecheck and build see types; test:unit is pure logic; test:integration is server-side; Closing reference check reads only the pull request's text. Nothing in the suite exercises a Query cache, so a minor that changes refetch or invalidation semantics goes green on all five checks and reaches the browser.
NEVER ALONE — Prisma client, adapter and CLI must stay in sync. platform.md: migration checksums live in _prisma_migrations and the migrations are hand-written SQL.
NEVER ALONE — the bundled Postgres image. platform.md: minimum v15 (NULLS NOT DISTINCT, ADR-0006), and a major needs a dump and restore, never a tag change (docs/development/postgres-upgrade.md).
NEVER ALONE — PDF generation. ADR-0046 §1 names the exact versions (pdf-lib 1.17.1, @pdf-lib/fontkit 1.1.1); font metrics and millimetres have to survive to paper.
NEVER ALONE — icons. ADR-0030: pinned, one dependency, and src/app/icons.tsx is its only importer.
NEVER ALONE — Markdown rendering and sanitising. ADR-0019: breaks: true, and a sanitising allowlist limited to the tags a listing may carry.
NEVER ALONE — image processing. storage-and-jobs.md: a native module in the scan path, taking a path so that nothing ever holds a card whole in memory.
NEVER ALONE — authentication. No written reason in the tree; on the user's instruction (2026-09-06), because it is the authentication library.

NEVER ALONE — the toolchain the build runs on: node is pinned in Dockerfile and in the setup-node steps of .github/workflows/ci.yml. pnpm is pinned once, in packageManager in package.json, and CI holds no pnpm version at all — pnpm/action-setup carries no version input and reads that field, as the Dockerfile's corepack enable does; platform.md states that derivation and it is not restated here. Grouped so the two node pins and the pnpm pin move in one pull request rather than three.
NEVER ALONE — one of the two storage backends (ADR-0011).

Every major waits for a person, whatever matched above. LAST on purpose: it is the safety net, so it must override every rule before it, including any future automerge rule someone adds without reading this file.
